# Existing-infrastructure deployment recipe

These files are a reviewable recipe, not a record of installation. No service, timer, cron, provider or process is installed by this branch. Run production only on an existing Linux application host with an approved persistent local filesystem, spare capacity, existing TLS ingress and Node 22. Do not put a new resident process on the Mac or Bot VM. Static hosting alone cannot run this API or worker.

1. Root pins and reviews this feature branch's implementation commit, checks the target host's existing Node 22 binary, service account, local disk headroom and free loopback port 8791. The recipes assume `/opt/neomorphic/current`, `/usr/bin/node`, and an existing `www-data` account. Adjust these three values to the actual existing application environment before installing. Read access to the repo and write access only to a dedicated store directory are required. `ProtectHome=true` means a checkout or Node binary under `/home` needs a reviewed adjustment. Keep `packages/change-monitor/src` and its Observatory vendor directory with the checkout. No install or build is needed.
2. Prepare `/var/lib/neomorphic-monitor` owned by that account, mode 0700, and `/etc/neomorphic-monitor/runtime.json`, mode 0600, readable by that account. Start from `runtime.example.json`. Keep `options.demo` and `mountedOrigin` absent. Configure ingress to terminate HTTPS and forward the dedicated monitoring prefix/host to `127.0.0.1:8791`, preserving `/v1` and `Authorization`. This service deliberately refuses non-loopback API binds and browser Origin headers. Do not change the gateway service or shared navigation to achieve this. Use the existing ingress owner's reviewed configuration outside this branch.
3. Generate distinct owner and reader credentials locally using the existing secret-management path. Put them in a private grant file (0600) outside the checkout, following `grant.example.json`. Never put a credential in a shell argument, URL, log or committed file. Provision from the pinned checkout:

   ```sh
   NODE_ENV=production /usr/bin/node services/continuous-monitoring/src/cli.mjs provision --config /etc/neomorphic-monitor/runtime.json --grant /private/path/customer-grant.json
   ```

   The command prints tenant id, plan, finite expiry and `charged: false`, never the credentials. Securely hand credentials to the tenant through the established channel. Keep the private grant in approved secret storage or remove it after secure enrollment. Rotating a grant replaces both credentials without resetting usage. `revoke --tenant <id> --config <file>` invalidates all tenant access and makes future ticks stop its monitors.
4. Render a focused unit preview using the actual existing paths/account (this only writes files):

   ```sh
   node services/continuous-monitoring/deploy/render-units.mjs --node /existing/node22 --repo /existing/repo --user existinguser --out /private/reviewed-units
   systemd-analyze verify /private/reviewed-units/neomorphic-monitor-api.service /private/reviewed-units/neomorphic-monitor-worker.service /private/reviewed-units/neomorphic-monitor-worker.timer
   ```

   Validate locally without installing a daemon: run the serialized package tests on the existing test host, then `tick --config <file>` once on the target. It does nothing with an empty store. Start `serve --config <file>` under the existing process supervisor only after the host configuration is reviewed. `/healthz` must return 200 and `/v1/manifest` must return the dedicated contract. Do not infer service acceptance from liveness alone.
5. On an already systemd-managed application host, review and install the three unit files; enable the API and timer through the existing deployment procedure. The timer starts the one-shot worker, which serializes its own observations and exits. Multiple accidental ticks are safe under the durable claim protocol; they do not double-fetch one slot. Limit host concurrency to one worker to conserve resources. Ten checks with the maximum request timeout can take about 100 seconds; the 15-second timer delay applies after completion. Capacity beyond that is unknown until measured; do not promise all 200 monitors a one-minute effective cadence. This recipe allocates no new server or provider charge.
6. Alternative on an existing cron-managed host: run `node .../src/cli.mjs tick --config ...` once a minute as the same account under a dedicated non-overlap `flock /var/lib/neomorphic-monitor/worker.lock`. Use either cron or the timer. With ten requests per tick and bounded deadlines, measured queue lag must fit the tenant schedule. Do not use a platform cron with an ephemeral filesystem or separate unshared database.
7. Add `maintenance --config <file>` through the existing daily maintenance job, plus a SQLite-consistent backup. Track disk/WAL size and restore a backup into a private test directory. Monitor only aggregate operational metrics: service health, last run timestamps, unknown runs, due lag, failed/exhausted deliveries, budget exhaustion, storage, known bytes/runtime and acknowledgement lag. There is no Prometheus endpoint or automatic pager in this branch. Tenant usage is available through the authenticated API.
8. Run a real production acceptance monitor against a customer-authorized, free, public, changing resource, then read and acknowledge its event through the public ingress. Record the actual production URL's public-safe identity, target deployment commit, worker schedule, measured latency and usage, and consumer readback. Only then should Root update public state, machine deploymentState and any reviewed offer/copy. The mounted-origin run in this branch does not satisfy this deployment acceptance.

For a paid entitlement, the authorized operator must verify an existing subscription through the existing billing process, then set `plan: "paid"`, an opaque `subscriptionRef` and a finite `entitlementUntil` in a private grant. Provisioning a paid entitlement does not create, verify, renew, invoice or charge that subscription. No checkout, billing webhook, receipt verification, automatic period reset or cancellation integration is implemented. Root must connect that seam before representing the service as an automatically billed subscription. A revoked/expired entitlement stops upstream observations; revoked credentials lose access while expired entitlements retain output inspection and acknowledgement until retention. Local maintenance still recovers/prunes outputs normally.

Rollback: disable this timer/cron entry, stop only this API, and keep the private database and consistent backup. Do not revert another owner's services or delete the store. An old dispatched request with no staged result remains unknown after restart, and its usage reservation is retained. Deployments must keep API and worker on the same schema/code version. SQLite schema v1 is additive and dedicated to this service; it does not touch correspondence, gateway or other jobs.
